frameworks.name: 10 Different Ways to Make a Million Dollars
frameworks.definition: A structured breakdown of ten distinct paths to generate a million dollars of value, each demonstrating value-creation or arbitrage mechanics that work at any revenue scale.

claims.text: You can make a million dollars by selling someone else five to ten million dollars of value and receiving one percent of that value created.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: The service increases a large-revenue-base company's conversion or revenue
You can articulate the value created (e.g., 5% lift on $100M revenue)
claims.mechanism: The larger the baseline asset you work with, the greater the absolute value of a percentage gain. A 5% lift on a $100M company ($5M incremental value) generates $1M+ commission.
bounded_by: Requires ability to execute the underlying work (e.g., conversion optimization, landing page redesign)
Does not apply to situations where the target company cannot quantify or measure the value created

claims.text: Real estate is fundamentally borrowing money to buy an asset and having someone else (tenant) pay off the debt you never had.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: You can secure a mortgage or financing
The property generates rental income sufficient to cover debt service
claims.mechanism: Tenant rent payments retire the debt obligation, transferring the cost burden from borrower to cash-flow generator. The borrower keeps appreciation and principal paydown benefit.

claims.text: You can purchase a residential property below market value, refinance at the higher appraised value, and pocket the difference without any out-of-pocket investment.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: You acquire the property at a significant discount (10-30% below market)
The bank is willing to finance based on the appraised market value rather than purchase price
You can qualify for the financing
claims.mechanism: Banks lend a percentage of appraised value (typically 75-80%), not purchase price. A $100k property purchased at $80k with a bank loan of $80k (at 80% LTV of $100k appraised value) yields the $20k difference.

numbers.axis: property acquisition discount and financing gap

anchors.region: Property purchased for $80k with $100k market value and 80% bank financing

bounded_by: Requires finding sellers willing to discount significantly
Requires bank appraisal to support the market-value valuation

claims.text: You can acquire a contract to purchase an asset at a future date at a predetermined price and then sell that contract to another buyer at a higher price without ever owning the asset.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: You have a contract/option on an asset at a locked price
A third party values that asset more highly than the contract price
The option period allows you to sell the contract before execution
claims.mechanism: You capture the spread between the option price and the buyer's perceived value without holding the underlying asset. The buyer gets the contract; you get the profit.
bounded_by: Requires a second buyer who agrees to take over the contract at a higher price
The underlying asset must actually be worth more than the option price for the buyer to accept

claims.text: You can earn a commission on expensive assets (real estate, commercial properties) by facilitating a transaction; on a $100M skyscraper at 3-4% commission, a single deal yields $3-4M without owning the asset.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: You have the ability or license to broker high-value asset sales
The transaction closes and commission is earned
claims.mechanism: High-value assets concentrate value into fewer transactions; a small commission percentage on a massive deal yields outsize returns compared to low-value asset sales.

numbers.axis: asset transaction size and commission percentage

bounded_by: Requires licensing or authorization to broker transactions in the relevant market

claims.text: You can generate a million dollars annually by solving the unit economics: $20,000 per week over 52 weeks (20 customers at $1,000 each, or 2 customers at $10,000 each, or 1 customer at $80,000 every four weeks).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: You have a consistent offer or subscription model
You can reliably acquire the target number of customers or units per week
claims.mechanism: The path to a million dollars is determined by three independent levers: price per unit, number of units sold, or frequency of repeat purchases. Adjust any lever to scale.

numbers.axis: annual revenue ($1M target) broken into weekly unit economics

anchors.region: 100 month membership ($100/mo, 10-month average duration) × 20 per week

claims.text: You can acquire multiple small information businesses (each doing ~$1M revenue) by offering to pay the owner their expected annual income for 2 years, combining them into one larger entity with superior economics due to overhead consolidation.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: The target businesses are small and the founders are willing to exit
You can identify multiple non-competing information businesses with similar target audiences
The combined entity has shared infrastructure (email list, fulfillment, support) that reduces duplicate costs
claims.mechanism: Overhead costs (marketing, customer support, fulfillment) do not scale linearly. Combining four $1M businesses into one $4M business with one marketing team and one fulfillment operation yields 2x+ profit margins compared to running them separately.

anchors.region: 4 businesses × $1M revenue, combined without consolidation benefit
Same 4 businesses consolidated with shared infrastructure

bounded_by: Founder cost is 2 years of owner income per business (e.g., $2M total cost for 4 businesses at $1M/yr each)
The businesses must be non-competing and serve overlapping audiences to achieve overhead consolidation

claims.text: You can earn affiliate income by honestly recommending products you have personally vetted to your audience; the audience saves time researching, you earn commission without product ownership or creation.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: You have an audience or platform that trusts your recommendations
The products you recommend genuinely solve problems for that audience
You disclose your affiliate relationship transparently
claims.mechanism: Your audience avoids the cost of evaluating 100 products when you shortcut to the single best option. That time savings is valuable to them; they willingly purchase through your link in exchange for the saved research effort.
bounded_by: Does not work if your audience perceives the recommendation as self-interested rather than curated for their benefit

claims.text: Arbitrage is buying something in one market at a lower price and selling it in another market at a higher price, capturing the spread. Works for cryptocurrency (buy at $19k in Japan, sell at $19.1k in US for $100 profit), lending (borrow at 1%, lend at 6%, keep 5% spread), and physical goods.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Two markets exist with different prices for the same good
You can execute the buy/sell transaction before prices converge
Transaction costs are lower than the price differential
claims.mechanism: Price differential between markets creates a profit opportunity. You exploit the spread by buying low and selling high across geographies or time periods.
bounded_by: Requires ability to move capital or goods between markets
Works only while price differential persists; arbitrage eliminates itself as more traders exploit the gap

claims.text: You must not constrain yourself by hourly thinking (how much per hour) but instead focus on providing value and taking a percentage of the value created, which is how high earners scale wealth rather than time.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: You are providing measurable value to a customer or business
You can articulate the value created in financial or quantifiable terms
claims.mechanism: Hourly thinking caps income at (hourly rate × hours available). Value-percentage thinking decouples income from personal time: if you create $10M in value and take 10%, you earn $1M regardless of hours spent.
bounded_by: Requires the ability to quantify and articulate value created
Does not apply to commoditized labor where customers do not perceive outcome-based value

claims.text: To get into something that will balloon in price (e.g., NFTs, pre-IPO investments, scarce resources with high demand), you must get in early when supply is scarce and demand is building, so that you capture appreciation before mainstream buyers enter.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: The asset is genuinely scarce or supply-limited
Demand is growing or will grow significantly
You can identify early before mainstream adoption
claims.mechanism: Early buyers face low competition for a scarce resource. As demand grows, more buyers bid against each other, driving prices up. Early positions benefit from this appreciation without additional contribution.
bounded_by: Does not guarantee appreciation; many early investments in scarce assets fail if demand does not materialize

examples.text: A buddy of Hormozi's got into real estate flipping houses, which initially seemed unprofitable due to effort and tenant management. He then bought a 14-unit apartment building with someone else's money (no personal capital), held it for four months, and sold it for $500k more than purchase price. This single success taught him that more expensive buildings generate proportionally larger absolute profits, leading him to transition to commercial real estate where he could flip 30-40 properties per year with just himself and a couple of VAs, buying at $10M and selling at $13M per transaction.

A friend of Hormozi combined four small information businesses (each doing approximately $1M annual revenue) by offering to pay each founder their annual income for two years rather than requiring immediate capital investment. He executed zero capital spend to acquire all four businesses. Once combined, he owned an asset generating $4M top-line and $1.5M bottom-line profit annually. He could then sell this combined entity for an estimated $5M, yielding $3M+ profit on zero capital investment.

practices.text: If you don't know how to create a specific value (e.g., increase e-commerce conversion rates), accept that you don't know how, commit to learning that skill, acquire the skill, and then you can sell it.

When seeking arbitrage opportunities or contract deals, talk to a large number of counterparties (e.g., building owners) to find the one outlier who is willing to transact at a significantly below-market price.

Be honest in affiliate recommendations; recommend products you have genuinely evaluated and believe in, positioning yourself as a time-saver for your audience rather than a self-interested salesperson.
